zh.summary: 先記住一句：LDAP 查到的是「這個身分，在這些搜尋條件下看得到的目錄資料」，不等於能修改物件或取得管理權限。

sourceBody.text: 10/26 午間：一次學一個核心概念
1. LDAP 是什麼？
LDAP（Lightweight Directory Access Protocol，輕量型目錄存取協定）讓程式查詢與操作目錄服務。
目錄像公司的組織通訊錄，依階層整理使用者、群組與資源。它可以用資料庫儲存，但「目錄服務」「底層資料庫」與「LDAP 協定」不是同一件事。Active Directory Domain Services（AD DS）是支援 LDAP 的目錄服務，不是 LDAP 的另一個名字。
LDAP 不只支援讀取，也支援修改；本課只談授權範圍內的唯讀列舉。[OpenLDAP 概覽](https://www.openldap.org/doc/admin26/intro.html)
2. 什麼時候用？
在已授權的帳號盤點、故障排除或安全檢查中，用來確認哪些帳號、群組與組織資訊可見。事前要確認目標、使用帳號、可查範圍及資料保存方式，不是能連上就能任意蒐集。
3. 看懂目錄與搜尋條件

items: Entry（項目）：目錄中的一個物件，例如一位使用者。
Attribute（屬性）：物件的欄位，例如 cn（常用名稱）、mail（電子郵件）。
DN（辨別名稱）：項目在目錄中的完整名稱，例如 cn=Mei,ou=People,dc=example,dc=test。ou 是組織單位，dc 是網域名稱的組成部分。
Base DN：搜尋從哪個項目開始，像先指定要查哪個部門。
Scope（範圍）：base 只查起點；one 只查直接下一層；sub 查起點及其所有下層。
Filter（篩選條件）：哪些項目符合要求，例如 (cn=Mei)。
回傳屬性：找到之後，要取回哪些欄位，不必把所有資料都拿走。

sourceBody.text: 因此，找到某個名稱，不代表已查完整個組織。結果還會受存取權限、數量及時間等限制。[RFC 4511 搜尋規格](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4511.html#section-4.5)
4. Bind、查詢權限與加密要分開
Bind 用來建立連線的身分／授權狀態，不是「一成功就有全部讀寫權限」。
匿名 Bind 成功，不代表匿名能列出人員；具名帳號認證成功，也不代表可以修改使用者或群組。實際可做什麼，要看存取控制。[RFC 4513](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4513.html#section-4)
常見的 TCP 389 可以用 StartTLS，在既有 LDAP 連線中啟用 TLS；TCP 636 的 LDAPS 則先建立 TLS，再交換 LDAP 訊息。

所以不能把「389」直接當成未加密，也不能只看到「636」就認定安全。要確認 TLS 確實成功、憑證與伺服器身分驗證正確；使用帳號密碼的 simple bind 不應在缺乏適當保護的連線上傳送。[Microsoft LDAP over TLS 說明](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/active-directory/enable-ldap-over-ssl-3rd-certification-authority)
5. 一個純合成、唯讀例子
假設你獲准用唯讀帳號查詢實驗室通訊錄：
搜尋起點：ou=People,dc=example,dc=test
範圍：one，只查 People 的直接下一層
條件：(cn=Mei)
要求欄位：cn、mail
假設回傳：
名稱 Mei，電子郵件 mei@example.test。
這只能證明：在這次身分、範圍與條件下，伺服器回傳了這個項目的指定資料。不能因此說已查完所有帳號、能讀密碼，或擁有網域管理權。
即使讀到群組成員關係，也還要確認特定資源的授權規則，不能直接當成實際有效權限。這是紙上例子，沒有連線查詢任何設備。

sourceBody.text: 6. 防護與證據判讀
防護重點是限制不必要的匿名讀取、採最小權限、保護連線與認證資訊，並依需要限制查詢來源及範圍。
紀錄查詢時間、實際身分、Base DN、Scope、Filter、要求欄位、完成狀態與筆數；不要保存密碼或不必要的個資。
要證明匿名資料暴露，應指出「匿名身分實際讀到了哪些資料」，不能只寫 Bind 成功。回傳零筆也不等於資料不存在，可能是範圍、條件、權限或查詢限制的影響。
小檢核：
匿名搜尋回傳零筆結果，為什麼不能直接寫「這個目錄沒有使用者」？請說出兩個還需要確認的因素。
一兩句即可。

en.summary: Remember: LDAP returns directory data visible to this identity under these search conditions. That does not establish permission to modify objects or administrator privileges.

sourceBody.text: October 26 midday: one core concept at a time
1. What is LDAP?
LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) lets programs query and operate on directory services.

A directory resembles an organizational contact list, arranging users, groups, and resources hierarchically. It may store data in a database, but a directory service, its underlying database, and the LDAP protocol are different things. Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) is a directory service that supports LDAP, not another name for LDAP.
LDAP supports modifications as well as reads; this lesson covers only read-only enumeration within an authorized scope. [OpenLDAP introduction](https://www.openldap.org/doc/admin26/intro.html)
2. When is it useful?

Authorized account inventories, troubleshooting, and security reviews use LDAP to determine which accounts, groups, and organizational information are visible. Confirm the target, account, permitted search scope, and data-retention arrangements beforehand. Connectivity alone does not authorize arbitrary collection.
3. Understanding directories and search conditions

items: Entry: an object in the directory, such as a user.
Attribute: an object's field, such as cn (common name) or mail (email).
DN (Distinguished Name): the entry's full name in the directory, for example cn=Mei,ou=People,dc=example,dc=test. ou means organizational unit; dc represents a domain component.
Base DN: the entry where a search begins, like specifying a department to examine first.
Scope: base examines only the starting entry; one examines only its immediate children; sub examines the starting entry and all descendants.
Filter: conditions that entries must match, such as (cn=Mei).
Returned attributes: the fields requested for matching entries; there is no need to collect everything.

sourceBody.text: Finding a name does not establish that the entire organization has been searched. Access rights, size limits, and time limits also affect results. [RFC 4511 search specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4511.html#section-4.5)
4. Separate Bind, query permissions, and encryption
Bind establishes the connection's identity/authorization state. Success does not grant all read and write permissions.

A successful anonymous Bind does not establish anonymous access to personnel listings. Successful named-account authentication does not establish permission to modify users or groups. Access controls determine permitted operations. [RFC 4513](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4513.html#section-4)
The common TCP 389 service can use StartTLS to enable TLS within an existing LDAP connection. LDAPS on TCP 636 establishes TLS before exchanging LDAP messages.

Port 389 alone does not establish unencrypted traffic, and port 636 alone does not establish safety. Confirm successful TLS, certificate validation, and server identity verification. A simple bind using an account name and password should not transmit them over a connection lacking appropriate protection. [Microsoft LDAP over TLS guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/active-directory/enable-ldap-over-ssl-3rd-certification-authority)
5. A purely synthetic, read-only example
Suppose you are authorized to query a laboratory directory with a read-only account:
Search base: ou=People,dc=example,dc=test
Scope: one, only the immediate children of People
Filter: (cn=Mei)
Requested attributes: cn, mail
Suppose the response contains:
Name Mei, email mei@example.test.

This establishes only that the server returned the specified data for this entry under this identity, scope, and filter. It does not establish a complete account inventory, password access, or domain administrator privileges.
Even visible group membership requires checking a particular resource's authorization rules before concluding effective access. This is a paper example; no device was queried.

sourceBody.text: 6. Defenses and evidence interpretation
Restrict unnecessary anonymous reads, apply least privilege, protect connections and authentication information, and restrict query sources and scope as appropriate.
Record the query time, actual identity, Base DN, Scope, Filter, requested attributes, completion status, and result count. Do not retain passwords or unnecessary personal data.

To establish anonymous data exposure, identify the data actually read anonymously, rather than merely recording a successful Bind. Zero results do not establish that data does not exist: scope, filters, permissions, or query limits may affect the response.
Quick check:
Why does an anonymous search returning zero results not justify saying that the directory has no users? Name two factors that still need checking.
One or two sentences are enough.
